newsitem.title: USA: AT&T details NCR operations, losses in filing.
newsitem.headline: AT&T details NCR operations, losses in filing.

text.p: AT&T Corp, in a filing on Thursday with the Securities and Exchange Commission, disclosed that net losses at its NCR Corp subisiary have totalled about $3.85 billion since 1993.
The filing, which relates to AT&T's planned spin-off of NCR, also states that during the last three and one-half years AT&T provided NCR with more than $2.82 billion in net cash contributions.
Of that amount, AT&T shifted $595 million to NCR in the first six months of 1996. The amount was $1.03 billion in 1995, $770 million in 1994 and $425 million in 1993.

According to the filing, AT&T said it plans to contribute another $419 million in cash plus whatever additional cash is needed to retire some $68 million in NCR debt, all prior to completion of the spin-off, which is due by year-end.
AT&T also said no one customer accounted for more than 10 percent of NCR's revenues but noted AT&T itself was NCR's largest customer for each of the last three years.

Including orders from Lucent Technologies Inc and other affiliates, AT&T accounted for eight percent of NCR's revenues in 1995, six percent in 1994 and five percent in 1993. For the first half of 1996, the share was eight percent.
Lucent has signed an agreement to for purchases totaling $150 million over the next three years from NCR. Lucent has already fulfilled $65 million under that agreement, according to the filing.
According to the filing, AT&T also plans to commit to a certain level of purchases but exact terms were not set out.

AT&T also noted that NCR's cost of capital most likely will increase after the spin-off because the computer company does not expect to be able to obtain financing on the favorable terms experienced by AT&T.
